correctness.rationale: A blank leaf can never see two colors. Fix an ordered pair of distinct final center colors c,d (six choices). On an m-leaf side its leaves must avoid its final center color. A center that is seeded with its own final color or independently forceable from its leaves contributes π_m=p^m[p·2^m+r(2^m−2)], with r=1−3p. A blank center that can only be forced after its neighbor is colored must have a constant leaf word on the third color, contributing r p^m: the constant word equal to the neighbor's color would still leave only one distinct neighbor color. Two mutually dependent unseeded centers cannot start. Thus for each final center pair exactly the contributions π_mπ_n, r p^m π_n and r p^n π_m occur, giving the frozen coefficients on expansion. These events produce proper final colorings; if both centers are already forceable from leaves, distinct target colors preserve the other force in either order, while equal targets prevent success. Thus no final center pair is double counted. At p=0 the probability is zero, at p=1/3 it is the uniform proper-coloring probability, and m=n=1 yields 24p³(1−2p). My replay enumerated all four initial states per vertex, including blank leaves, and all legal orders for the sixteen m,n pairs from 1 through 4; no success-order dependence occurred and the exact coefficients matched, including (48,144,96) for m=n=2.
residual_risks: The finite replay corroborates the proof and is not a substitute for the all-m,n argument. No claim for other color counts or arbitrary trees.

value.rationale: The double star is the natural first two-adjacent-hub test extending the known path and local leaf-attachment formulas to branching. The exact coefficients resolve both genuinely nonlocal effects: a neighboring hub can enable a force, and two attempted forces can conflict. The formula gives a check for any tree recursion or bound on forced-coloring success, including highly unequal branching and the no-seed case; it is not just a restatement of the ordinary chromatic polynomial or a single small graph calculation.
residual_risks: No general tree recursion or new complexity bound is demonstrated.
